title: Two different stories. One competition!
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/ca2aa0673e1e44bebcc568e49dab624d/images/acc2340fd13449d987a2945c91a627cbe10%20copy%201.jpg)![44747355de6f46d497960eda381521f7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/ca2aa0673e1e44bebcc568e49dab624d/images/44747355de6f46d497960eda381521f7La%20Diez%20by%20Tinu%20Jose%20%283%29.png)  
🔟 **LA DIEZ — The Number 10**  
Inspired by Argentina’s iconic football heritage and the legendary **No. 10** , _La Diez_ explores how football identity can be translated into contemporary fashion. The design combines Argentina’s signature sky-blue palette with a sporty, feminine silhouette and details inspired by the visual language of football jerseys.  
  
![db71da2dd7dc4e29b209267c6c66f10c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/ca2aa0673e1e44bebcc568e49dab624d/images/db71da2dd7dc4e29b209267c6c66f10c10%20copy.jpg)  
🌊 **LA MAREA — The Tide**  
Inspired by Portugal’s deep connection with the Atlantic Ocean, _La Marea_ translates the rhythm and movement of ocean tides into a contemporary football lifestyle jersey. The flowing print, wave-like details, and deep burgundy palette are designed to capture the energy of the sea while keeping the design rooted in football culture.  
  
**LA MAREA — The Tide:** <https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/dc3551c95db1457f9064aaa92ccd2ea3>  
**LA DIEZ — The Number 10:**<https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/3395307d69a54886808af29047c17a07>  
  
Both projects were created in **CLO 3D** , with the aim of blending football culture, fashion, storytelling, and digital garment design.

Would love to hear what you think!  
**Which one speaks to you more — LA MAREA or LA DIEZ?**

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: LA DIEZ👍🏻
Reply 1: Glad it caught your eye!❤️
content_description: Showcasing innovative digital fashion designs that blend football culture and storytelling through the inspired collections LA DIEZ and LA MAREA.

title: Problem with Glasses Registration
content:
Hi, I need your help.

I created these glasses, as you can see in the first image.

I registered them, but the lenses appear black in the render even though they use the same material. Does anyone know how I can fix this issue?![30c923ff47c64468ac7ca2a452948ebd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/fe4036a6eb0f4e0c99177d53d2461142/images/30c923ff47c64468ac7ca2a452948ebdScreenshot%202026-08-09%20110609.jpg)![cfdeaf5f900d418a82ad28d97a716abf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/fe4036a6eb0f4e0c99177d53d2461142/images/cfdeaf5f900d418a82ad28d97a716abfScreenshot%202026-08-09%20110428.jpg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you for following up and for your guidance. I’ll give it a try and let you know how it goes.

Comment 2: Hi, I just tested this on several pattern pieces and glasses, with various results. So it is not clear to me what is causing the issue. At first, I suspected the difference in Absorption for both examples, but I have also produced an opaque pattern piece with the standard settings, so now I am confused. The only thing I can detemrine so far is that it appears to be connected to the color, all my examples work on #FFFFFF, but also NOT all of the ones on #D3B673 turn out opaque. I will investigate further and get back to you! (Unless one of my colleagues here has another idea?)
Reply 1: So far, I've determined that in order to display colored glass properly, Thick Textured Surface has to be toggled on. However, this should not affect your glasses. Are the glasses transparent when the color is set to white/none? (#ffffff)
content_description: Seeking help to resolve a rendering issue where registered glasses lenses appear black despite using the correct material.
